open_case_m6.conclusion: NONE. The sample is consistent with Spec S~_m = [-m,m], but coverage of an interval by a finite sample is not the equality, and in particular it does not show that the two eigenvalue branches MEET -- the obstruction the paper identifies. No claim is made.

Q^v has rank 3 = m-1 and acts freely with finitely many orbits on both graphs (Lemma 2.2, text:127-145)
girth K(4) = 6, girth S~_4 = 4 (Theorem 1.4; both by the edge-deletion algorithm, and exp2 cross-checks them by exhaustive cycle enumeration and explicit cycles)

girth 6 vs 6: an isomorphism preserves the girth, so the two graphs are NOT isomorphic (Theorem 1.5)  <-- INJECTED ERROR: S~_4 girth reported as 6, so the separator is vacuous and the non-isomorphism claim is NOT supported; this check catches that
explicit 6-cycle in K(4): all consecutive pairs adjacent, all 6 vertices distinct
explicit 4-cycle in S~_4 (s_1 and s_3 commute, m >= 4): all consecutive pairs adjacent, all 4 vertices distinct

both spectra attain exactly the same endpoints -4 and +4 (at the identity character the cell matrix is the genuine adjacency matrix of an m-regular graph); K range [-4.000000, 4.000000], S~_4 range [-4.000000, 4.000000].  Interval FILLING is not re-checked here: exp1 covers K(m) and exp3 covers S~_m

over 4 characters (the identity plus 3 random ones) the K cell 2x2 spectrum and the S~_4 cell 12 x 12 spectrum both lie in [-4, 4]; a single eigenvalue outside would be a counterexample to the inclusion, but this is a 4-character sample
A_chi is Hermitian to < 1e-12 at every sampled character, so the eigenvalues used above are the eigenvalues of a genuine self-adjoint cell operator

the cell V_K/Q^v has 2 vertices (Lemma 3.1), the cell W_a/Q^v has 24 = 4! vertices, so the two voltage graphs are not isomorphic either -- but note a cell is relative to the chosen period lattice, so this is structural information, not by itself a graph invariant
